newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Monterey sees Q1 net income $15-16 mln.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Monterey sees Q1 net income $15-16 mln.

text.p: Monterey Resources Inc, the largest heavy crude oil producer in California, which was spun off from Santa Fe Energy Resources Inc in November 1996, expects to report net income of $15-$16 million in the first quarter of 1996 and cashflow of $25-26 million, chief executive Graham Whaling said.

"In spite of refinery turnarounds in California, we expect to report net income of $15-16 million. We have been able to get $16.00 a barrel for the oil we sold in the first quarter," Whaling told Reuters in an interview on Thursday.
Monterey made $14.4 million net income in the fourth quarter of 1996, its first quarter as an independent company.

Whaling told Reuters that demand for heavy crude in California continued to be strong, that there was more demand than supply and that in any case Monterey would continue to be the lowest cost supplier for California refineries.

"There is an excess of refining capacity on the west coast. They need our crudes and if you want to import there is a cost impact of $1.00-$3.00 per barrel. Our fields are linked by pipeline to major refineries," Whaling said.
He said that Monterey had not been affected by the wave of refining mergers which is sweeping the U.S.
"I would like to see refiners achieving better margins. As things stand they are going to try to put pressure on the price they pay for heavy crude," he said.
Monterey is looking to either buy or form a joint venture to produce more heavy crude, Whaling said.
"If it were to be in Canada it would be a joint venture around Saskatchawen and Alberta," he said.
The company is also looking to buy natural gas producing assets with output of 20 million cubic feet (mcf) per day to cut its costs.

"With natural gas at $4.40 per mcf in January this year, this is a huge cost for us as we use it to create steam for our extraction. We would either buy gas we could use ourselves or use the gas as a hedge and sell it," Whaling said.

He said that the company had raised production to 50,000 barrels of heavy oil per day in the first quarter and had expanded its drilling program to attempt to prove up some of the estimated 3.0 billion barrels of oil which have not been classed as proved or probable in its oilfields.
The company has planned capital expenditure of $75 million for 1997. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
